picks.file: Giusto de Menabuoi - Veduta di Padova nel trecento - Basilica di Sant Antonio - Cappella del Beato Luca Belludi.jpg
picks.what: View of Padua in a fresco in the Basilica of Sant’Antonio (Belludi chapel)
picks.why: the walled medieval city painted from life; trimmed off the saint and fresco border

picks.file: Padua en de Ponte de Graici over de Brenta Veduta della Città di Padova al Ponte de Graic (titel op object) Le delicie della Brenta (serietitel) Les delices de la Brenta (serietitel) Gezichten op de rivier de Brenta , RP-P-1965-147.jpg
picks.what: Padua from the Ponte dei Graici on the Brenta, etching in Gianfrancesco Costa, Le delizie del fiume Brenta
picks.why: true general view; skyline with the domes of the Santo and towers; trimmed to the plate

picks.file: Rudolf von Alt Basilika San Antonio in Padua 1836.jpg
picks.why: color, high resolution; the city’s signature landmark with Donatello’s Gattamelata

picks.file: View of Padua from La Specola.jpg
picks.what: View from La Specola over the old town to the cathedral, photograph
picks.why: sunny panorama of the historic center; cathedral and canal visible

gaps: P1: only a flat city plan (#6) and a map of the walls (#4); #7 is a 19th-century lithograph misdated 1545. P2: only Canaletto’s Imaginary View of Padua (a capriccio, #8–#13), skipped as not a true view. P4: the photochroms are Mission San Antonio de Padua in California; Grubacs (#24) is dated only ‘before 1878’. P5: nothing.
notes: If a P2 view is wanted, Canaletto’s Imaginary View of Padua (#8, 1741–44, very high resolution) combines Paduan buildings but is invented. Guardi’s Prato della Valle (#16, 1760s, color) is a good alternative for P3 but only 1052 px wide.
